component.name: scp
component.title: SCP
component.description: Copy files to remote hosts using the secure copy protocol (SCP).
component.label: file

lazyStartProducer.label: producer
lazyStartProducer.description: Whether the producer should be started lazy (on the first message). By starting lazy you can use this to allow CamelContext and routes to startup in situations where a producer may otherwise fail during starting and cause the route to fail being started. By deferring this startup to be lazy then the startup failure can be handled during routing messages via Camel's routing error handlers. Beware that when the first message is processed then creating and starting the producer may take a little time and prolong the total processing time of the processing.

autowiredEnabled.label: advanced
autowiredEnabled.description: Whether autowiring is enabled. This is used for automatic autowiring options (the option must be marked as autowired) by looking up in the registry to find if there is a single instance of matching type, which then gets configured on the component. This can be used for automatic configuring JDBC data sources, JMS connection factories, AWS Clients, etc.

verboseLogging.label: advanced
verboseLogging.description: Whether to log the INFO messages of JSch at INFO level. JSch logs much at INFO level, so by default the component logs these messages at DEBUG level. The component passes the JSch log messages, with the [JSCH] prefix, to its own logger.

healthCheckConsumerEnabled.label: health
healthCheckConsumerEnabled.description: Used for enabling or disabling all consumer based health checks from this component

healthCheckProducerEnabled.label: health
healthCheckProducerEnabled.description: Used for enabling or disabling all producer based health checks from this component. Notice: Camel has by default disabled all producer based health-checks. You can turn on producer checks globally by setting camel.health.producersEnabled=true.

producerIn.description: The content of the file: text, bytes, a stream or a file, which is read into memory first to send its size. A Map or a List fails: marshal it first

producerOut.description: Unchanged, with the name of the remote file in the CamelFileNameProduced header

disconnect.label: common
disconnect.description: Whether or not to disconnect from remote FTP server right after use. Disconnect will only disconnect the current connection to the FTP server. If you have a consumer which you want to stop, then you need to stop the consumer/route instead.

checksumFileAlgorithm.label: producer
checksumFileAlgorithm.description: If provided, then Camel will calculate a checksum from the file that has been written, and store the result in the CamelFileChecksum header.

chmod.label: producer
chmod.description: The permissions of the file that the producer writes, as three octal digits, for example 644. Any other value is replaced by 664. The producer sends it in the scp protocol line of the file, and the remote scp uses it when it creates the file. The directories that the producer creates for a file name with a path get 775.

fileName.description: Use Expression such as File Language to dynamically set the filename. For consumers, it's used as a filename filter: only a file with exactly this name is consumed, as the name is not a pattern (use antInclude or include to consume the files that match a pattern). For producers, it's used to evaluate the filename to write. If an expression is set, it take precedence over the CamelFileName header. (Note: The header itself can also be an Expression). The expression options support both String and Expression types. If the expression is a String type, it is always evaluated using the File Language. If the expression is an Expression type, the specified Expression type is used - this allows you, for instance, to use OGNL expressions. For the consumer, you can use it to filter filenames, so you can for instance consume today's file using the File Language syntax: mydata-${date:now:yyyyMMdd}.txt. The producers support the CamelOverruleFileName header which takes precedence over any existing CamelFileName header; the CamelOverruleFileName is a header that is used only once, and makes it easier as this avoids to temporary store CamelFileName and have to restore it afterwards.

jailStartingDirectory.label: common
jailStartingDirectory.description: Used for jailing (restricting) writing files to the starting directory (and sub) only. This is enabled by default to not allow Camel to write files to outside directories (to be more secured out of the box). You can turn this off to allow writing files to directories outside the starting directory, such as parent or root folders. For consumers that use a localWorkDirectory, this also restricts the downloaded files to stay within the configured localWorkDirectory.

checksumWriteFile.label: producer
checksumWriteFile.description: If checksumFileAlgorithm has been configured then this option controls whether to write a checksum file as well or not. The checksum file will always be written in the same folder as the original file.

flatten.label: producer
flatten.description: Flatten is used to flatten the file name path to strip any leading paths, so it's just the file name. This allows you to consume recursively into sub-directories, but when you eg write the files to another directory they will be written in a single directory. Setting this to true on the producer enforces that any file name in CamelFileName header will be stripped for any leading paths.

allowNullBody.label: producer,advanced
allowNullBody.description: Used to specify if a null body is allowed during file writing. If set to true then an empty file will be created, when set to false, and attempting to send a null body to the file component, a GenericFileWriteException of 'Cannot write null body to file.' will be thrown. If the fileExist option is set to 'Override', then the file will be truncated, and if set to append the file will remain unchanged.

disconnectOnBatchComplete.label: producer,advanced
disconnectOnBatchComplete.description: Whether or not to disconnect from remote FTP server right after a Batch upload is complete. disconnectOnBatchComplete will only disconnect the current connection to the FTP server.

lazyStartProducer.label: producer,advanced
lazyStartProducer.description: Whether the producer should be started lazy (on the first message). By starting lazy you can use this to allow CamelContext and routes to startup in situations where a producer may otherwise fail during starting and cause the route to fail being started. By deferring this startup to be lazy then the startup failure can be handled during routing messages via Camel's routing error handlers. Beware that when the first message is processed then creating and starting the producer may take a little time and prolong the total processing time of the processing.

moveExistingFileStrategy.label: producer,advanced
moveExistingFileStrategy.description: Strategy (Custom Strategy) used to move file with special naming token to use when fileExist=Move is configured. By default, there is an implementation used if no custom strategy is provided

browseLimit.label: advanced
browseLimit.description: Maximum number of messages to keep in memory available for browsing. Use 0 for unlimited.

connectTimeout.label: advanced
connectTimeout.description: Sets the connect timeout for waiting for a connection to be established Used by both FTPClient and JSCH

soTimeout.label: advanced
soTimeout.description: Sets the so timeout FTP and FTPS Is the SocketOptions.SO_TIMEOUT value in millis. Recommended option is to set this to 300000 so as not have a hanged connection. On SFTP this option is set as timeout on the JSCH Session instance.

timeout.label: advanced
timeout.description: Sets the data timeout for waiting for reply Used only by FTPClient

caSignatureAlgorithms.label: security
caSignatureAlgorithms.description: A comma-separated list of the signature algorithms that are accepted for the CA signature of an OpenSSH host certificate, for example ssh-ed25519,rsa-sha2-512. The CA keys are the cert-authority entries of the known hosts file. If not set, the JSch default list is used, which does not accept the SHA-1 based ssh-rsa.

certBytes.label: security
certBytes.description: The OpenSSH user certificate as a byte array, for certificate-based authentication. Only used together with privateKeyFile or privateKeyBytes, and when neither certFile nor certUri is set.

certFile.label: security
certFile.description: The OpenSSH user certificate file for certificate-based authentication, for example id_ed25519-cert.pub. A path on the file system, or with the classpath: prefix a resource on the classpath. Only used together with privateKeyFile or privateKeyBytes, the private key of the certificate. Takes precedence over certUri and certBytes.

certUri.label: security
certUri.deprecationNote: Use certFile, which loads the certificate in the same way and takes precedence.
certUri.description: The OpenSSH user certificate for certificate-based authentication, loaded the same way as certFile: a path on the file system, or with the classpath: prefix a resource on the classpath. Only used together with privateKeyFile or privateKeyBytes, and when certFile is not set. Takes precedence over certBytes. Deprecation note: Use certFile, which loads the certificate in the same way and takes precedence.

knownHostsFile.label: security
knownHostsFile.description: The known hosts file that JSch checks the key of the remote host against when the producer connects, in the OpenSSH known_hosts format. A path on the file system, or with the classpath: prefix a resource on the classpath. An cert-authority entry lets the producer accept an OpenSSH host certificate signed by that CA. What happens with a host that is not in the file, or whose key changed, depends on strictHostKeyChecking.

preferredAuthentications.label: security
preferredAuthentications.description: A comma-separated list of the SSH authentication methods to try, in order of preference, for example publickey,password. JSch supports gssapi-with-mic, publickey, keyboard-interactive and password. If not set, the JSch default gssapi-with-mic,publickey,keyboard-interactive,password is used.

privateKeyBytes.label: security
privateKeyBytes.description: The private key as a byte array, for public key authentication. Only used when privateKeyFile is not set. Use privateKeyFilePassphrase for an encrypted key.

privateKeyFile.label: security
privateKeyFile.description: The private key file for public key authentication. A path on the file system, or with the classpath: prefix a resource on the classpath. The key must be in a format that JSch reads, such as OpenSSH, PEM or PuTTY. Takes precedence over privateKeyBytes. Use privateKeyFilePassphrase for an encrypted key.

privateKeyFilePassphrase.label: security
privateKeyFilePassphrase.description: The passphrase of an encrypted private key of privateKeyFile or privateKeyBytes. Not needed for a key that is not encrypted.

strictHostKeyChecking.label: security
strictHostKeyChecking.description: Sets whether to use strict host key checking. Setting this to 'no' (the default) disables host key verification and makes the connection vulnerable to man-in-the-middle attacks. Use 'yes' in production environments.

useUserKnownHostsFile.label: security
useUserKnownHostsFile.description: Whether to use the known hosts file of the user, the .ssh/known_hosts file in the home directory (the user.home system property, or the HOME environment variable), when knownHostsFile is not set. If that file does not exist, or if false and knownHostsFile is not set, no host is known, and strictHostKeyChecking decides whether the producer connects.

ciphers.label: security,advanced
ciphers.description: A comma-separated list of the ciphers for the SSH connection, in order of preference, for example aes128-ctr,aes256-ctr. The cipher names are those of JSch. If not set, the JSch default list is used.
